title: Finite models and good representatives for normalized integral scalar comparisons
statement: Let ell be prime, E and L finite extensions of Q_ell, and iota:E→L an embedding. Use the ordinary scalar functors [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension, lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition] and the strict finite pullback and tensor models [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]. For every n the unique natural finite pullback map sends 1 tensor f*(1 tensor x) to f*(1 tensor (1 tensor x)); the unique finite tensor map sends 1 tensor ((1 tensor x) tensor (1 tensor y)) to (1 tensor (1 tensor x)) tensor (1 tensor (1 tensor y)). Their consecutive reduction equations assemble unique strict tower maps and the specified diagonal Roos chain maps. Ordinary scalar extension preserves the good complexes (termwise flat and K-flat). The diagonal Roos map is the coordinate-normalized additive comparison [def-sf-additive-roos-map]. This is the unchanged finite-model part formerly in IntegralOperationsScalarComparisons, not a new derived comparison.

proof.text: Apply the two finite-level existence-and-uniqueness lemmas to obtain the normalized natural chain maps at every n, on all complexes and pairs of complexes. Their displayed generator equations are exactly the pullback and tensor equations of this statement.

proof.text: The two consecutive reduction lemmas apply to these natural maps with their proved generator equations. For an arrow m→n with m≥n, iterate consecutive squares: the case m=n is the identity square; the case m+1→n is the composite of the consecutive square m+1→m with the inductively established square m→n. Thus the level maps define strict tower transformations. Naturality is componentwise in the input complexes. Any other transformation with these level components is equal by equality at each n; finite-level uniqueness therefore also gives the claimed normalized tower uniqueness. This is the retained scalarTowerAssembly argument.

source.place: section-tensor-product and lemma-tensor-product-pullback; project ScalarRoosComparison.lean scalarTowerAssembly; sites-cohomology.tex lemma-pullback-K-flat; derived.tex definition-derived-limit.

proof.text: For either tower C and its transformation a, define the specified chain map to be κ_(S,C) followed by Roos(a). The first factor is exactly the two-coordinate additive Roos map of the cited definition; the second is the Roos functor applied to the strict tower transformation. Composition defines the claimed diagonal chain map, without choosing a map of triangles or claiming that scalar extension preserves arbitrary products.

source.place: section-tensor-product and lemma-tensor-product-pullback; project ScalarRoosComparison.lean scalarTowerAssembly; sites-cohomology.tex lemma-pullback-K-flat; derived.tex definition-derived-limit.

proof.text: Ordinary scalar extension is termwise sheaf change of rings along j_W:R_(E,W)→R_(L,W). Its concrete complex has terms R_(L,W)⊗P^i and differential 1⊗d_P. Hence the object and morphism formulas identify it as a complex, not merely degreewise, with the change-of-rings complex. Apply the cited K-flat change-of-rings theorem to a good P: its hypotheses are precisely K-flatness and flatness of every term. It gives both properties over R_(L,W); the complex identification transfers K-flatness and its degree components transfer flatness. The independent-universe tensor-colimit theorem says these sheaf tensor functors preserve colimits in the module universe even when the site object and Hom universes differ. The retained ordinary pullback normalization is an equation using these good representatives and the specified chain map; no further derived comparison is asserted.
